data.cultural_impact: The name Wadid holds great significance in Islamic culture as it embodies the beautiful concept of receiving a great gift or blessing. This can be interpreted in various ways, such as being blessed with excellent abilities or being born into a prosperous family. The name serves as a reminder of the many blessings and gifts bestowed upon individuals by Allah, and encourages people to be grateful for the blessings they have been given.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Wadid signifies the belief that every human being is a unique creation of Allah, endowed with special talents and abilities. This name inspires individuals to recognize and cultivate their God-given talents, and to use them for the betterment of themselves and society. It also serves as a reminder of the ultimate gift given by Allah - the gift of faith and the opportunity to lead a pious and righteous life. The name Wadid encourages us to be thankful for the blessings we have received, and to strive towards living a life that honors and utilizes our unique talents and abilities in the best possible way for the pleasure of Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir records Wadid ibn al-Abras as a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and a participant in the Battle of Uhud.
Al-Biruni describes Wadid as a sage, scholar, and poet in the Islamic world during the Abbasid Caliphate, particularly noted for his work in astronomy and mathematics.
